title: Grade 9 Science — The Fundamental Unit of Life (Cell)
description: Cell structure, organelles, plant vs animal cells, cell division basics
subject: science

questions.question: Who first observed and named cells?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke first observed and named cells in 1665 while examining thin cork slices under a primitive microscope. The word 'cell' comes from the Latin 'cellula' meaning small room.

questions.question: Cell theory states that:
options: Only animals are made of cells
All living organisms are composed of cells and cells arise from pre-existing cells
Cells can be created from non-living matter
Only complex organisms are made of cells
questions.explanation: Cell Theory (Schleiden, Schwann, Virchow): (1) All living things are made of cells; (2) Cell is the basic unit of life; (3) All cells arise from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula e cellula).

questions.question: The control centre of the cell containing genetic information (DNA) is the:
questions.explanation: The nucleus is the control centre of the cell — it contains DNA (chromosomes), directs cell activities, and is bounded by a nuclear membrane with pores. It controls protein synthesis and cell division.

questions.question: Which organelle is called the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are called the powerhouse of the cell because they generate most of the cell's supply of ATP (energy) through cellular respiration. They have their own DNA (semi-autonomous).

questions.question: Chloroplasts are found in:
options: Plant cells and some algae cells
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are found in plant cells and algae (not in animal cells). They contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis, converting light energy into chemical energy (glucose).

questions.question: The cell wall in plant cells is mainly made of:
questions.explanation: The plant cell wall is primarily composed of cellulose — a complex carbohydrate. It provides rigidity and structural support. Fungal cell walls are made of chitin; bacterial cell walls of peptidoglycan.

questions.question: Which of the following is present in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
options: Cell wall and large central vacuole
questions.explanation: Plant cells have: cell wall (cellulose), chloroplasts, and a large central vacuole. Animal cells lack all three. Both have: cell membrane, mitochondria, nucleus, ribosomes, etc.

questions.question: The Golgi apparatus is responsible for:
options: Packaging and transporting proteins and lipids to their destinations
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus (Golgi body) processes, packages, and dispatches proteins and lipids received from the endoplasmic reticulum to their destinations (secretion, cell membrane, lysosomes).

questions.question: Lysosomes are often called 'suicide bags' because they:
options: Contain digestive enzymes that can break down the cell itself if ruptured
Break down DNA in old cells
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that digest cellular waste, foreign material, and worn-out organelles. If they rupture (e.g., in disease), these enzymes digest the cell itself — hence 'suicide bags'.

questions.question: The fluid inside the cell surrounding all organelles is called:
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm is the jelly-like fluid filling the cell (between the cell membrane and nucleus). It contains organelles, salts, enzymes, and organic molecules. Nucleoplasm is the fluid inside the nucleus.

questions.question: Osmosis is defined as the movement of water molecules through a semi-permeable membrane:
options: From a region of low concentration to high concentration
From a region of higher water concentration (lower solute) to lower water concentration (higher solute)
Always from inside the cell to outside
Against a concentration gradient using energy
questions.explanation: Osmosis: movement of water (solvent) molecules through a semi-permeable membrane from a region of higher water (lower solute) concentration to lower water (higher solute) concentration. It is passive (no energy).

questions.question: When a cell is placed in a hypertonic solution, it will:
questions.explanation: Hypertonic solution has higher solute (lower water) concentration than the cell. Water moves OUT of the cell by osmosis → cell shrinks. In plant cells this is called plasmolysis; in RBCs, crenation.

questions.question: Prokaryotic cells differ from eukaryotic cells in that prokaryotic cells:
options: Have no membrane-bound nucleus or organelles
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes (bacteria, archaea) lack a membrane-bound nucleus — their DNA is in a region called the nucleoid. They also lack membrane-bound organelles (no mitochondria, ER, Golgi). Eukaryotes have all these.

questions.question: Ribosomes are the site of:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis — they translate mRNA into protein. They are found on the rough endoplasmic reticulum (attached) or free in the cytoplasm. Present in all cells.

questions.question: The process by which white blood cells engulf bacteria is called:
questions.explanation: Phagocytosis ('cell eating') is a process where cells engulf large particles (bacteria, dead cells) by surrounding them with the cell membrane. White blood cells (neutrophils, macrophages) use this for immunity.
